3.text: adopted son-in-law. Such a son-in-law is called by the Chukchee vaˊta iˊtɪlɪn

4.text: (“continuous dweller”). I have already spoken of the poor young men of

5.text: Reindeer or Maritime extraction who come to the rich reindeer-breeders and

6.text: serve them as assisting herdsmen. The larger part of them marry into the

7.text: family of the master and become adopted sons-in-law. Some present them-

8.text: selves as suitors from the very beginning. Others, who have not yet decided

9.text: to sacrifice their freedom, begin as herdsmen, and try to become acquainted

10.text: with the family and its life before occupying the position of suitors.¹

11.text: As stated before, the suitor must work very hard, and undergo all kinds

12.text: of privations; and, naturally enough, the young men want to look more care-

13.text: fully into the quality of the possible reward. Much depends also on the future

14.text: prospects of the girl in question. Some masters have a daughter to dispose

15.text: of; others, only a niece, or a poor kinswoman living in their family in the

16.text: position of a female servant. Marriage with such a girl does not promise

18.text: Be this as it may, the time of trial of the candidate for a son-in-law is

19.text: considerably shorter than the serving-time of an independent suitor. It changes

20.text: also in accordance with the individual conditions of the adopting family. If

21.text: the family has several grown-up daughters and at the same time is short of

22.text: male hands, the poor suitor may be then and there adopted and given matri-

23.text: monial rights over the girl. Still, after that he has to work hard and be

24.text: correct and successful in everything, at least for the first two or three years.

25.text: The wife is given to him in order to make his attachment stronger, but the

26.text: family does not take on themselves any obligations toward him. Even after

27.text: his wife has borne him a child, if he begins to give occasion for displeasure,

28.text: he may be sent away without much ado;² or, after a whole year spent in

29.text: the family, he may suddenly feel displeased himself, and go away, leaving

30.text: behind him his wife and even the child. Only after a stay of several years,

31.text: when his work has left its mark on the common herd, and perhaps he has

32.text: some reindeer marked with his own ear-mark, does his position become more

33.text: stable, and then he receives a voice in the family affairs.

35.text: son-in-law. For instance, in the tale already quoted,³ the young new-comer,
